<!-- pr-reviewer: 0ba6098385b18957e1fa8879421638ca4840cd0b -->
Needs changes before merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes geometry. It adds no dependencies, UI changes, or process files.

The reader keeps units explicit and bounds input size and counts. Both DXF suites pass. One additional geometry test fails.

Requested before merge:

1. **Preserve the endpoints of small bulge arcs, or refuse them.** See [crates/geometry/src/dxf/entities.rs:127-135](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/0ba6098385b18957e1fa8879421638ca4840cd0b/crates/geometry/src/dxf/entities.rs#L127-L135). A two-vertex LWPOLYLINE from `(0, 0)` to `(0.00001, 0)`, with bulge `1e-17`, passes the range and sweep checks. The returned arc has center `(5e-6, 250000000000.00003)`, radius `250000000000.00003`, start angle `-1.5707963267948966`, and sweep `4e-17`. Adding the sweep does not change the start angle in `f64`. Both reconstructed endpoints are `(2.0308084989341915e-5, 0)`. Thus, accepted geometry loses the source endpoints and collapses under endpoint evaluation. The current guard checks only zero and full-circle sweeps. Check that the arc representation preserves the source endpoints. Return a named error when it cannot. Add a regression test for this input and its clockwise form.

The failing test calls the public `parse` function with these bytes:

```rust
b"0\nSECTION\n2\nENTITIES\n0\nLWPOLYLINE\n90\n2\n10\n0\n20\n0\n42\n1e-17\n10\n0.00001\n20\n0\n0\nENDSEC\n0\nEOF\n"
```

It evaluates each endpoint as `(center.x + radius * angle.cos(), center.y + radius * angle.sin())`. The end angle is `start_angle + sweep_angle`.

```text
assertion `left != right` failed: two distinct DXF vertices became the same arc endpoint
  left: (2.0308084989341915e-5, 0.0)
 right: (2.0308084989341915e-5, 0.0)
```

Local build and test results:

- Trial merge with upstream/main `3580f388821d604e602728495a53df1881889b0d`: clean. The PR already contains this main commit.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: completed. It selects batch because geometry changed. This was a plan check, not a batch run.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf`: 15 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf_refusals`: 15 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Additional `accepted_bulge_must_preserve_distinct_endpoints` test: failed at runtime. It ran in a separate temporary Cargo project against the unchanged PR library. The failure also occurs with dependency versions from the workspace lock file.

I repeated two mutations from the author's inventory:

- `common_z`: disabling the common-elevation guard made `dxf_varying_z_within_and_between_entities_is_refused` fail at runtime. Restoring the guard made it pass.
- `coordinate_range`: disabling the coordinate-range guard made `dxf_nonfinite_and_out_of_range_geometry_is_refused` fail at runtime. Restoring the guard made it pass.

All temporary mutations were restored. The worktree has no source changes. No goldens moved, so no golden lines needed review. No GitHub runner was used. GUI import, downstream machining, Windows, macOS, and the full batch gate were not exercised in this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Fixed the small bulge endpoint finding.

The reader reconstructs both endpoints from the arc representation. It refuses the arc if either error exceeds `1e-10` of the source chord length. The error names the entity and the endpoint failure.

- `dxf_bulge_arcs_that_lose_source_endpoints_are_refused` pins the supplied input and its clockwise form. It covers both polyline formats and distinct but displaced endpoints.
- `dxf_bulge_sign_and_major_arcs_keep_the_exact_sweep` also checks ordinary small arcs in both directions.

Mutation check: guard removed -> RED for all eight cases; guard restored -> GREEN.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. It selected batch coverage. All 10 steps passed.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.

New head: `e5204e0ef315584f32f4a699589c118f22abe4f1`.

Please re-review this head.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review because the PR changes geometry. The previous endpoint finding is resolved on this head.

The reader checks both reconstructed bulge endpoints against the source chord. It returns a named error when it cannot preserve them. The new test covers the reported input, both arc directions, both polyline formats, and displaced endpoints. Ordinary small arcs still pass. Input limits, explicit units, and named refusals remain in place.

I read all changed source files, both test suites, the decision record, and issue #1860. The bulge convention and unit codes agree with the published [VERTEX reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0741E831-599E-4CBF-91E1-8ADBCFD6556D.htm) and [HEADER reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A85E8E67-27CD-4C59-BE61-4DC9FADBE74A.htm).

Local results:

- Trial merge with upstream/main `3580f388821d604e602728495a53df1881889b0d`: clean. The PR already contains this commit.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: passed. It selects a 10-step batch plan. This was a plan check, not a batch run.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf`: 16 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf_refusals`: 15 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

I repeated three mutation checks myself:

1. Disable the endpoint guard: `dxf_bulge_arcs_that_lose_source_endpoints_are_refused` fails at runtime and lists all eight accepted bad cases. Restore the guard: GREEN.
2. Disable `common_z`: `dxf_varying_z_within_and_between_entities_is_refused` fails at runtime. Restore the guard: GREEN.
3. Disable `coordinate_range`: `dxf_nonfinite_and_out_of_range_geometry_is_refused` fails at runtime. Restore the guard: GREEN.

All temporary mutations were restored. The worktree has no source changes. No goldens moved, so no golden lines required review. The PR changes no UI, dependency, build script, workflow, or process file.

Requested before merge: none.

No GitHub runner was used. GUI import, downstream machining, Windows, macOS, and the full batch gate were not exercised in this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
